title: Multiplication and divisibility as lattice addition and order
classical_object: integer multiplication, divisibility, gcd, and lcm
pvg_object: finite-support valuation vectors with addition and coordinate order
forward_map: nu(mn)=nu(m)+nu(n); d|n iff nu(d)<=nu(n); nu(gcd)=min; nu(lcm)=max
reverse_map_or_loss: lossless when prime-coordinate labels are retained
lost_structure: none for multiplicative data; additive order is not represented
analytic_transform: none required for the exact algebraic bridge

title: Divisor boxes and Dirichlet convolution
pvg_object: integer box below nu(n) and additive decompositions beta+gamma=nu(n)
lost_structure: none multiplicatively; ordering of divisors as integers is not geometric
analytic_transform: Dirichlet series converts convolution to multiplication in a common absolute-convergence domain
hypotheses: finite-support valuations; convergence hypotheses for the analytic transform

title: Coordinate factorization and Euler products
classical_object: multiplicative functions, Dirichlet series, and Euler products
pvg_object: coordinate-axis observables and product of local generating functions
forward_map: a multiplicative function is determined by prime-power axis values; its Dirichlet series factors into local coordinate series where justified
reverse_map_or_loss: local factors recover prime-power coefficients; a formal product without convergence does not certify an analytic function
lost_structure: global analytic continuation, pole, zero, and boundary information are not supplied by geometry
analytic_transform: sum_alpha F(alpha) exp(-s ell(alpha)); Euler product under factorization and convergence
hypotheses: multiplicativity plus absolute convergence, or an explicitly stated formal-series setting
classification: Known analytic bridge with convergence gate

title: Size ranges as weighted valuation half-spaces
classical_object: n<=x, short intervals, and weighted arithmetic sums
pvg_object: ell(nu(n))<=log x and thin weighted slabs
forward_map: log n=ell(nu(n)); size restrictions become weighted lattice regions
reverse_map_or_loss: lossless for exact labeled lattice points, but coarse geometric summaries lose integer order and additive neighborhood information
lost_structure: successor order, additive spacing, phase, and short-interval correlations unless separately encoded
analytic_transform: weighted lattice Laplace/Dirichlet sum; estimates require counting or analytic input
hypotheses: positive integers; explicit boundary convention for intervals
classification: Exact identity with explicit order-loss warning

title: Boolean support geometry and the Möbius function
classical_object: squarefree integers and the Möbius function
pvg_object: Boolean valuation points and support parity
forward_map: mu(n)=0 off the Boolean cube; on it mu(n)=(-1)^|supp nu(n)|
reverse_map_or_loss: lossless for squarefreeness and Möbius value when labels and support are retained
preserved_structure: squarefree condition, support cardinality, convolution inverse role
lost_structure: support-only summaries may discard prime labels and logarithmic size
analytic_transform: sum mu(n)n^-s=1/zeta(s) in its valid domain; sum mu(n)^2 n^-s=zeta(s)/zeta(2s)
hypotheses: Re(s)>1 for the stated absolutely convergent Dirichlet series identities

title: Residue fibers and character Fourier coordinates
classical_object: reduced residue classes, Dirichlet characters, and fiber variance
pvg_object: valuation points carrying modular prime labels, projected to arithmetic fibers
forward_map: reduced-class indicators decompose by character orthogonality; principal subtraction isolates non-principal coordinates; Parseval converts fiber energy to character second moments
reverse_map_or_loss: all character coefficients recover a function on the reduced residue group; second moments alone lose phase and individual-character identity
preserved_structure: finite group Fourier data and L2 energy
lost_structure: phase after energy aggregation; residue is not recoverable from unlabeled exponent multisets
analytic_transform: finite Fourier transform and character Dirichlet/L-functions
hypotheses: reduced residues, fixed normalization, and explicit treatment of the principal character
classification: Known exact Fourier bridge / normalization diagnostic

title: Sieve visibility, aggregation loss, and certificates
classical_object: divisibility data through level D, Type-I aggregates, and sieve remainders
pvg_object: truncated valuation profile followed by an aggregation map
forward_map: indicators 1_{d|n}, d<=D, are equivalent pointwise to nu^(D)(n); family sums A_d are a further pushforward
reverse_map_or_loss: pointwise truncated data is recoverable from all divisibility indicators, but aggregate A_d generally has a nontrivial kernel
preserved_structure: visible prime-power depths and selected divisibility moments
lost_structure: individual profiles, sign, phase, order, correlations, and target purity after aggregation
analytic_transform: sieve main term plus remainder and level-of-distribution certificates
hypotheses: specified sequence, sieve level, weights, main-term model, and remainder norm
literature_status: classical sieve information recast as a loss audit
classification: Exact pointwise bridge plus diagnostic aggregation-loss principle

title: From valuation observables to summatory asymptotics
classical_object: Dirichlet series, Perron inversion, contour shifts, and Tauberian transfer
pvg_object: Laplace transform of a valuation-lattice observable
forward_map: D_F(s)=sum_alpha F(alpha)exp(-s ell(alpha)); analytic information can be transferred to summatory functions by a named theorem
reverse_map_or_loss: coefficients determine the Dirichlet series in convergence regions, but geometry alone does not provide continuation, poles, zero-free regions, growth, or contour bounds
preserved_structure: coefficients, multiplicative factorization, singularity-to-main-term routing when hypotheses hold
lost_structure: all analytic certificates not explicitly proved
analytic_transform: Dirichlet/Laplace transform followed by Perron, Tauberian, Selberg-Delange, or contour tools
hypotheses: the exact convergence, continuation, growth, boundary, and error assumptions of the selected transfer theorem
classification: Known conditional transfer interface; not a theorem without hypotheses
